_LOCKED: Printed Montessori materials use the Montessori Picture Bank and NOTHING ELSE: docs/picture-bank/photos/<word>/<word>.jpg — photoreal studio photographs of one concrete holdable object on WHITE. Decided Jul 2026. Rules and the selection criteria live in docs/picture-bank/HANDOFF_PICTURE_BANK_Jul23.md.
_fit: These photos are shown object-fit:contain on white, never cover. A 1344x896 saw cropped to a square loses the ends of the saw. Matches swap-picture-bank-images.py, which already swaps the packs to object-fit:contain;background:#fff.
_twoTracks: Shelf / 3-part cards = photoreal object on white. Circle + lesson Dark Phonics = googly-eye characters and forest-green spotlit art. NEVER MIX THEM. The Dark Phonics art is not lower quality, it is for a different job; a 3-part card has to answer a child's 'what is this?' about an object they can hold.
_noToys: Added Jul 26 2026 after ambulance/taxi/panda/penguin were caught rendered as a die-cast toy car, a die-cast toy car, a plush stuffed animal, and a vinyl figurine respectively — the audit script only checks background/size/contrast, never subject material, so these passed --audit and shipped. Rule: real objects and real animals only, even for subjects that can't literally be held (a full-size ambulance, a live panda) — use a realistic full-size photograph or a true-to-life scale-model photograph, never anything styled as a children's toy (no die-cast cars, no plush/stuffed animals, no vinyl or resin figurines). The one sanctioned exception is infant, which uses a doll by design (see HANDOFF_PICTURE_BANK_Jul23.md — photographing a real, identifiable child isn't appropriate picture-bank content) — but that doll must read unambiguously as a toy doll, not a hyperrealistic 'reborn' doll indistinguishable from an actual baby. Full incident writeup: docs/handoffs/HANDOFF_PICTURE_BANK_Jul26.md.
_round3AIGenerationAbandoned: Added Jul 26 2026 (same day, later). The Midjourney regeneration described in _noToys DID NOT actually fix the problem — verified by pulling the live files straight from Storage after they were 'fixed' and screenshotting them: ambulance and taxi were still glossy die-cast-proportioned toy cars, panda was still an unmistakable plush stuffed toy, penguin was still a vinyl/resin figurine, and infant had reverted to a photoreal human baby again. Two full rounds of Midjourney generation with explicit anti-toy prompt language failed to produce a genuinely real-reading image for these five specific subjects — the model's training bias toward cute/toy-styled renders for 'ambulance', 'taxi', 'panda', 'penguin', and 'baby' subjects on a clean background is strong enough that prompt engineering alone did not overcome it, and self-review by screenshot-checking the final output (not just trusting the audit script or a generation-time glance) is what actually caught it both times. FIX: abandoned AI generation for these five words entirely. Replaced with real photographs sourced from Wikimedia Commons (public domain / CC-licensed, verified via EXIF camera data or explicit 'toy producer' captions to be genuine, not AI-generated) — ambulance: Ford Transit AMR ambulance, CC BY-SA 3.0; taxi: London Hackney Carriage black cab, CC0; panda: Smithsonian National Zoo's Ling Ling, CC BY 4.0; penguin: African penguin on a beach, CC0; infant: Simba Toys 'Calineczka' baby doll, CC BY-SA 3.0. Each was re-verified live from Storage via a fresh browser screenshot (cache-busted URL) after publishing, not assumed correct from a script success message. Lesson for next time: don't trust an AI-generation 'fix' for a toy-bias problem without opening the actual final file — and don't trust a prior session's handoff doc that says a fix shipped without independently re-checking the live asset.
